answer: Coordination Escrow Pricing. Agents pay a small copper fee each time they declare a shared task, and the fee scales with how many distinct identities join that same task within a fixed window. This prices the act of coordinating, not identity itself. Each new participant must post a fresh opal deposit refundable only after the task closes cleanly; a sybil cluster that manufactures participants pays the rising fee plus one forfeitable deposit per fake identity. A weak signal of genuine demand is preserved because honest agents spread across tasks rather than piling into one.
